# EQTL3.SA (Equatorial S.A.) Technical Analysis, as of 2026-08-31

## Bottom line

EQTL3.SA is in a short-term recovery inside a longer downtrend. Momentum has turned up, but the stock is still below its 50- and 200-day averages, and it has lagged the Ibovespa badly. For the next 20 sessions (entry at the Sep 1, 2026 close, exit about Sep 29), I see **no clear edge versus ^BVSP, with a slight lean toward underperformance** unless the rebound clears the 50-day average on rising volume. The rest of this report explains the evidence and what would change the view.

## Verified data (source of truth)

The verified snapshot for 2026-08-31 shows:

- **OHLCV:** Open 37.18, High 37.40, Low 36.67, Close 36.67, Volume 10,352,300 (vs. a 20-session average of about 11.95M).
- **Indicators:** 10 EMA 36.389; 50 SMA 38.048; 200 SMA 39.633; RSI 48.23; Bollinger middle 36.332, upper 39.261, lower 33.403; MACD -0.439; MACD signal -0.694; MACD histogram +0.254; ATR 0.956.
- **Relative performance vs ^BVSP:** 5 sessions +0.94% vs +3.21% (-2.27 pts); 20 sessions -5.71% vs -0.33% (-5.38 pts); 60 sessions -5.00% vs +5.19% (-10.19 pts); 120 sessions -11.98% vs -3.29% (-8.69 pts).
- **Beta** to ^BVSP over 120 sessions: 1.26, correlation 0.81.

I checked every indicator I pulled separately (10 EMA, 50 SMA, 200 SMA, MACD, MACD histogram, RSI, ATR, VWMA) against the snapshot. They match. I did not pull the Bollinger series separately, so those values come only from the snapshot. No discrepancies were found.

## Trend structure

**Longer-term:** The stock peaked near 45.35 on 2026-04-15 (the April high was 46.32 intraday on 2026-04-17). It then fell steadily. The 50 SMA is now 38.05 and has declined from 38.84 on 2026-08-03. The 200 SMA is flat at about 39.63, so the 50 SMA sits below it, which is a bearish configuration. The close is about 3.6% below the 50 SMA and about 7.5% below the 200 SMA.

**Recent swing:** Closes fell from 39.21 on 2026-08-04 to 34.23 on 2026-08-17, a drop of roughly 13% in nine sessions. The stock then rebounded to 37.15 on 2026-08-25 and has since drifted back to 36.67. Price now sits just above the 10 EMA but below the Bollinger middle band's 20-day value of 36.33 by only a small margin.

**Interpretation:** The move since mid-August looks like a sharp correction followed by a partial retracement. It is not yet a confirmed trend reversal. The stock has not reclaimed any of the three moving averages that are now overhead.

## Indicator-by-indicator read

**Moving averages.** Price is above the 10 EMA (36.39), which is a short-term positive. It is well below the 50 SMA (38.05) and the 200 SMA (39.63). The 10 EMA turned up on 2026-08-21 (35.57) and has risen since. That is a short-term signal only. The 50 SMA's downward slope is the key constraint.

**MACD.** The MACD line (-0.44) is still below zero, but it crossed above its signal line (-0.69) around 2026-08-25. The histogram went from -0.013 on 2026-08-24 to +0.130 on 08-25, peaked at about +0.254 on 08-28, and has been flat since (+0.254 on 08-31). Momentum has stopped improving, which is a warning sign. Because the MACD is still below zero, this is a counter-trend bounce signal, not a full bullish trend signal.

**RSI.** RSI fell to about 25.0 on 2026-08-17, which is oversold, and recovered to 51.8 on 08-25. It is now 48.2, neutral. The rebound has not pushed RSI into overbought territory, so there is room to run, but it has also not shown strong buying pressure. A move above 55 would be a stronger sign.

**Volatility and Bollinger Bands.** ATR is 0.96, about 2.6% of price per day. Over 20 sessions, that is a rough one-sigma range of about ±4.3% (√20 × 0.96 / 36.67 ≈ 11.7%, but the per-day ATR is a poor guide to multi-week moves; treat this as an order-of-magnitude estimate). The upper band (39.26) and lower band (33.40) are about 7% above and 9% below the current price. The bands have widened during the August sell-off and are now starting to narrow, which points to decreasing volatility.

**Volume and VWMA.** Volume spiked during the sell-off: 12.4M on 2026-08-13, 22.1M on 08-14, 19.4M on 08-17, 19.6M on 08-18, and 18.2M on 08-20. The rebound happened on lower volume: 9.2M on 08-25, 8.2M on 08-26, 6.4M on 08-27, 11.9M on 08-28, and 10.4M on 08-31. A bounce on falling volume is less convincing than a sell-off on heavy volume. The VWMA (35.42) sits below the close, meaning the volume-weighted average price is lower than the current price. That is consistent with heavy selling at lower prices, and the stock now needs to rebuild its volume-weighted base above that level.

## Relative strength vs. Ibovespa

This is the most important consideration for your horizon. The stock has underperformed by 5.4 points over 20 sessions and 10.2 points over 60 sessions. With a beta of 1.26, the stock tends to amplify index moves, so an index rally would likely lift it, but the recent pattern shows it falling more than the market during the sell-off. The 5-session relative result (-2.3 pts) shows that the rebound has also lagged the index. Unless the index falls sharply, the stock must generate its own outperformance to beat ^BVSP.

## Key levels (from verified data)

| Level | Price | Why it matters |
|---|---:|---|
| Resistance: 50 SMA | 38.05 | Below it, the medium-term trend is still down. |
| Resistance: upper Bollinger band | 39.26 | Upper edge of the current range. |
| Resistance: 200 SMA | 39.63 | Long-term trend benchmark. |
| Support: Bollinger middle / ~10 EMA | 36.33 to 36.39 | Current area; a close below it would weaken the bounce. |
| Support: Aug 17 low | 34.23 (close) | Recent swing low; a retest is possible if the bounce fails. |
| Support: lower Bollinger band | 33.40 | Mechanical lower bound. |

## Scenarios for the next 20 sessions

**Constructive case:** The stock closes above 38.05 (50 SMA) on rising volume (above about 12M). The MACD histogram keeps rising and RSI moves above 55. This would point toward a retest of 39.3 to 39.6. Relative performance would likely improve.

**Neutral case (base case):** The stock trades between 36.3 and 38.0 with falling volume. The MACD histogram flattens near zero. The stock roughly tracks the index but does not outperform.

**Bearish case:** The stock closes below 36.33 and then below 34.23 (the August low) with rising volume. This would reopen the lower Bollinger band at 33.40 and extend underperformance.

## Actionable guidance for the 20-session horizon

- **Lean:** No strong call. The short-term momentum is improving, but the trend structure and relative weakness argue against a long position versus the index. If you must hold a position, treat it as a tactical bounce trade, not a trend trade.
- **Entry trigger for a long:** A daily close above 38.05 with volume above the 20-session average (about 11.9M).
- **Risk control:** Use an ATR-based stop, roughly 1.5 to 2 ATR below entry (about 1.4 to 1.9 BRL below), or a close below 34.23 if you want a structure-based stop.
- **Watch for:** A histogram roll-over below zero, RSI failing near 50 again, or another high-volume down day. Any of these would signal that the bounce is failing.
- **Calendar note:** Brazilian market holidays (for example, Sep 7) will shift the exit date. Count actual trading sessions when setting the exit.

## Caveats

- The tools provide price and volume data only. I have no fundamental, news, or dividend-policy data. The stock's April 8 jump (41.09 to 43.15, about +5%) and its August decline may have fundamental or regulatory causes that these indicators cannot explain. The August drop coincided with heavy volume, so a company-specific event is possible.
- The dividend column shows 1.45 BRL on 2025-11-06 and 0.133 on 2025-12-30. The price data here is not explicitly dividend-adjusted, so verify return calculations against an adjusted series before relying on them.
- No historical backtest of these signals was run. The support and resistance levels above are read from current indicator values, not validated against past bounces.

## Summary table

| 10 EMA | 36.39; price slightly above | 2026-08-31 | Short-term positive |

| 200 SMA | 39.63; price about 7.5% below; flat | 2026-08-31 | Long-term negative |
| MACD / signal | -0.44 / -0.69; bullish cross about 08-25 | 2026-08-25 | Early momentum turn, still below zero |
| MACD histogram | +0.254, flat since 08-28 | 2026-08-31 | Momentum plateauing |
| RSI | 48.2 (low 25.0 on 08-17; high 51.8 on 08-25) | 2026-08-31 | Neutral; room to move higher |
| Bollinger bands | Middle 36.33, upper 39.26, lower 33.40 | 2026-08-31 | Bands narrowing; range 33.4 to 39.3 |
| ATR | 0.96 (about 2.6% of price) | 2026-08-31 | Moderate daily volatility |
| VWMA | 35.42; price above | 2026-08-31 | Volume-weighted base below price |
| Volume | Sell-off 18 to 22M; rebound 6 to 12M | 08-13 to 08-31 | Bounce on weaker volume |
| Relative to ^BVSP | -5.4 pts (20d), -10.2 pts (60d); beta 1.26 | 2026-08-31 | Persistent underperformance |
| Key resistance | 38.05 / 39.26 / 39.63 | Current | Needed for a trend change |

# EQTL3.SA (Equatorial S.A.): News and Macro Report, as of 2026-08-31

**Bottom line:** Little company-specific news this week, and nothing that clearly moves the stock over a 4-week horizon versus the Ibovespa. The two items that matter are the early-stage Echoenergia sale process (a possible deleveraging catalyst) and falling-earnings optics. The rate backdrop is modestly supportive for a leveraged utility. I lean neutral on EQTL3 relative to ^BVSP, with low conviction. I did not retrieve price or volume data, so this call has no technical input.

## 1. Company news (CVM filings and Brazilian press, 24–31 Aug 2026)

**Filings to CVM:**
- **26 Aug, annual tariff adjustment (RTA) for Equatorial Maranhão.** ANEEL approved it on 24 Aug, effective 28 Aug. The average consumer effect is +5.76% (high voltage +8.68%, low voltage +5.25%). Parcel B (the regulated revenue base) rose 2.53% to R$2,767.8m. The filing says the adjustment reflects 4.7% cumulative inflation, net of a 1.54% X-factor, and includes the new contractual terms from the May 2026 concession renewal. The increase is a clean, regulated, cash-generating event. The Parcel B increase is modest, however, and the headline tariff rise is mostly pass-through.
- **27 Aug, 2Q26 institutional presentation.** Key figures:
  - LTM net revenue R$55.1bn; LTM adjusted EBITDA R$11.8bn.
  - Market cap R$49.04bn at 30 Jun 2026; share price R$38.94 at 2Q26.
  - Distribution RAB R$34.9bn across 14.8m consumers in seven DisCos.
  - 1,777 MW renewables (1,204 MW wind, 573 MW solar).
  - Reference stakes: 15% of SABESP and 30% of COPASA, plus full control of CSA.
  - About R$900bn of sanitation investment needed nationally. The pipeline includes an auction of about R$18.7bn in Maranhão in 4Q26, and smaller auctions in 3Q26.

**Press:**
- **28 Aug, InfoMoney/Brazil Journal/Reuters: Echoenergia sale process.** Equatorial has reportedly started selling its renewables subsidiary Echoenergia. Engie (EGIE3) is among groups preparing due diligence. The process is early. Echoenergia was bought in 2021 for about R$10bn enterprise value. The CEO had said in March that the company was open to asset recycling. The deal is unconfirmed by the company. A signed sale within 4 weeks is unlikely; the more likely effect is headline sentiment.
- **24 Aug, BB Investimentos (2Q26 review):** Distribution peers, including EQTL3, showed operating progress from market growth and tariff adjustments. The high investment load and high interest rates still limit deleveraging.
- **24 Aug, Squadra (fund manager):** Equatorial is one of the fund's main holdings, alongside Meli, Nubank and Energisa. Squadra's funds trailed the Ibovespa in 1H26 (Long-Only –6.2% versus +6.8% for the index), so this is a conviction signal from one manager, not a catalyst.

**Earnings trend (from the 2Q26 presentation, a key risk):** Net income (ex-minorities) has fallen sharply. It was R$2,812m in 2024, R$1,586m in 2025 and R$866m on an LTM basis at 2Q26. Adjusted EBITDA is steadier, at about R$11.8bn LTM. The gap is largely financial and depreciation costs. The market may weigh the earnings decline more than the EBITDA stability.

## 2. Macro backdrop (Banco Central do Brasil data)

| Indicator | Latest | Trend / context |
|---|---|---|
| Selic target | 14.00% (31 Aug) | Easing: 15.00% in early March, 14.75% in March, 14.50% in April–May, 14.25% in June–July, 14.00% in August. |
| Focus Selic, year-end 2026 (median) | 13.75% | Drifted down from 14.00% in late June. |
| Focus Selic, year-end 2027 (median) | 12.00% | Market expects roughly 175bp more in cuts through 2027. |
| Focus Selic, year-end 2028 (median) | 10.50% | Continued easing expected. |
| IPCA 12m | 4.44% (July print) | Peaked at 4.72% in May; easing since. |
| USD/BRL (PTAX) | 5.18 (31 Aug) | Up from 5.08 at end-July. Modest BRL weakness this month. |

**Read-through for EQTL3:**
- **Supportive:** Falling Selic expectations lower financing costs for a highly leveraged distributor and reduce the discount rate applied to regulated cash flows. Inflation is easing, which helps the IPCA-indexed tariff base. The 2027–28 cut path is the main tailwind, and it is already partly priced in.
- **Neutral to negative:** A weaker BRL raises the cost of USD-linked debt and imported equipment. The move is small (about 2% this month) but worth monitoring.
- **Relative-to-index angle:** Utilities are defensive and rate-sensitive. In a rate-cut tape they often outperform the cyclical-heavy Ibovespa. In a risk-on rally led by commodities or banks, they often lag. The Ibovespa's composition therefore matters for the excess-return outcome.

## 3. Global and prediction-market inputs

- **Global news:** The news feed returned no results for 24–31 Aug, and the tool notes it only serves recent items. I cannot assess US or global risk sentiment for this week. Another source should check it.
- **Prediction markets:** The tool withheld Brazil election odds for 2026-08-31, because it serves live odds only and would leak post-decision information. The Brazilian election cycle is a real risk for the Ibovespa and the BRL, so this is a gap in my analysis.

## 4. Assessment for the 4-week horizon (versus ^BVSP, dividend-adjusted)

**Positives:**
- Regulated tariff resets are being applied on schedule (Maranhão, 28 Aug).
- Falling Selic expectations support a leveraged utility's valuation and funding costs.
- Possible asset recycling via Echoenergia could reduce leverage. This is an option, not a sure event.
- Sanitation auctions (3Q26 and 4Q26) are potential growth catalysts.

**Negatives:**
- Net income has collapsed (R$2.8bn in 2024 to R$0.9bn LTM). Earnings-driven investors may stay away.
- Deleveraging remains constrained by heavy capex and high rates, as the BB review notes.
- The BRL has weakened modestly this month.
- No near-term company catalyst is scheduled within 4 weeks that I can identify.

**Call:** Neutral versus ^BVSP, low conviction. Expected excess return is close to zero. The main upside risk is a faster Echoenergia sale or a positive rate surprise. The main downside risk is a risk-on rally in cyclicals, or a sharp BRL move. A tilt to overweight would need price-momentum confirmation, and an underweight would need a clearer earnings-deterioration signal.

## Key points summary

| Area | Item | Date | Signal for EQTL3 (4-week view) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Company | Maranhão RTA +5.76% (Parcel B +2.53%) | 24–28 Aug | Neutral to positive: on-schedule regulated resets | High |
| Company | Echoenergia sale process started (Brazil Journal/Reuters) | 28 Aug | Positive if it closes; early stage, so mostly headline risk | Medium |
| Company | 2Q26 deck: LTM net income R$0.87bn (2024: R$2.8bn) | 27 Aug | Negative: earnings deterioration weighs on sentiment | High |
| Company | Sanitation auctions (3Q26 and 4Q26, incl. Maranhão R$18.7bn) | Upcoming | Positive medium-term; timing uncertain | Medium |
| Company | Squadra lists EQTL3 as a top bet | 24 Aug | Mildly positive; single-manager signal | Low |
| Macro | Selic 14.00%, cut from 15.00% in March | 31 Aug | Positive for leveraged utility valuation | High |
| Macro | Focus Selic 2026 13.75%, 2027 12.00% | 28 Aug | Positive: further cuts expected, partly priced in | Medium |
| Macro | IPCA 12m 4.44% (down from 4.72% peak) | Jul | Mildly positive for IPCA-indexed tariffs | Medium |
| Macro | USD/BRL 5.18, up about 2% in August | 31 Aug | Mildly negative via USD debt and capex costs | Medium |
| Data gap | Global news and Brazil election odds unavailable | 31 Aug | Unknown; a key risk to the Ibovespa and BRL | — |
| **Overall** | **Neutral versus ^BVSP** | **Horizon ~20 sessions** | **Low conviction; no price data used** | **Low** |

evidence.text:
# EQTL3.SA (Equatorial S.A.) Fundamental Report

**As of 2026-08-31.** Figures are R$ millions unless noted, from CVM filings (DFP annual, ITR quarterly) as filed.

## Data availability caveat

- **Company profile and valuation:** `get_fundamentals` withheld its output for this date. The vendor serves only present-day values, so market cap, P/E, 52-week range, and sector labels are unavailable. No valuation multiple can be computed here.
- **Insider transactions:** withheld. The vendor dates trades by when they happened, not when they were filed, so I cannot tell which trades were public on 2026-08-31.
- **Available data:** the CVM statements below. The 2025 Q4 and 2025 Q2 quarterly income figures are not directly reported; some are derived.

## 1. Income statement

| Period | Revenue | Gross profit | Gross margin | EBIT (pre-fin.) | EBIT margin | Financial result | Pre-tax | Tax | Net income (cont.) | Net income (total) | EPS (R$) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q3 2025 (Jul–Sep) | 14,145.1 | 3,486.7 | 24.7% | 2,391.7 | 16.9% | -1,573.6 | 818.1 | -208.3 | 609.8 | 609.8 | 0.374 |
| FY 2025 | 52,073.8 | 13,607.3 | 26.1% | 8,136.9 | 15.6% | -5,681.9 | 2,455.0 | -421.8 | 2,033.2 | 2,503.9 | 1.334 |
| Q1 2026 (Jan–Mar) | 12,749.9 | 3,455.0 | 27.1% | 2,324.6 | 18.2% | -1,504.0 | 820.6 | -213.9 | 606.8 | 606.8 | 0.338 |
| Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun) | 13,738.9 | 3,616.0 | 26.3% | 2,514.4 | 18.3% | -1,669.6 | 844.8 | -191.8 | 653.0 | 653.0 | 0.386 |
| H1 2026 (derived) | 26,488.8 | 7,071.0 | 26.7% | 4,839.0 | 18.3% | -3,173.6 | 1,665.4 | -405.7 | 1,259.8 | 1,259.8 | 0.724 |

**Observations:**
- **Operations are steady and improving.** EBIT margin rose from about 16.9% in Q3 2025 to about 18.3% in both 2026 quarters. Gross margin held near 26–27%.
- **Financial expense absorbs most of the operating profit.** The financial result runs at roughly -R$1.5 to -1.7bn per quarter, about 65–70% of EBIT. Pre-tax income is only about a third of EBIT.
- **Net margin is thin.** Quarterly net margin is about 4.8%.
- **2025 earnings are inflated by a one-off.** The R$2,503.9m total includes R$470.7m from discontinued operations. Continuing operations earned R$2,033.2m, so the underlying run-rate is lower than the headline EPS of R$1.334 implies.
- **Tax rate is volatile.** Effective rates were about 17% for FY2025, 26% in Q1 2026, and 23% in Q2 2026.
- **Run-rate.** H1 2026 annualizes to roughly R$2.5bn net income and about R$1.45 EPS. Quarterly revenue of R$12.7–13.7bn compares with a 2025 quarterly average of about R$13.0bn, implying modest top-line growth. Year-over-year quarterly growth cannot be computed because the 2025 quarterly comparatives are not in the data.

## 2. Balance sheet

| Date | Total assets | Current assets | Current liabilities | Current ratio | Non-current liabilities | Total liabilities | Equity | Liabilities / equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-09-30 | 126,167.1 | 32,667.4 | 20,859.4 | 1.57x | 72,511.2 | 93,371 | 32,796.5 | 2.85x |
| 2025-12-31 | 109,603.9 | 26,605.0 | 17,803.9 | 1.49x | 63,472.1 | 81,276 | 28,327.9 | 2.87x |
| 2026-03-31 | 111,792.0 | 27,293.7 | 17,523.2 | 1.56x | 66,069.4 | 83,593 | 28,199.3 | 2.96x |
| 2026-06-30 | 118,944.1 | 26,308.2 | 16,749.9 | 1.57x | 73,478.8 | 90,229 | 28,715.3 | 3.14x |

**Observations:**
- **Leverage is rising.** Liabilities/equity went from 2.85x to 3.14x in three quarters. Non-current liabilities rose about R$10bn in H1 2026 alone, from 63.5bn to 73.5bn.
- **Liquidity is adequate.** The current ratio is stable around 1.5x. Current liabilities fell slightly while non-current debt rose, so the new borrowing is longer-dated.
- **Equity fell despite profits.** Equity dropped from R$32.8bn to R$28.7bn over the period, about R$4.1bn, even though H1 2026 net income was about R$1.26bn. Dividends, buybacks, or other equity movements probably explain the gap, but the filings provided do not show which.
- **Asset base is growing.** Total assets rose from R$109.6bn to R$118.9bn in H1 2026, mostly non-current, consistent with capital deployment.
- **Gross debt is not separated** in the data provided, so net debt/EBITDA cannot be computed directly.

## 3. Cash flow

| Period | Operating CF | Investing CF | Financing CF | Net change in cash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY 2025 | 3,973.9 | -2,865.1 | -1,755.3 | -646.5 |
| 9M 2025 | 2,733.4 | -7,132.4 | 5,954.1 | 1,555.1 |
| Q1 2026 | 683.8 | 606.0 | 1,718.3 | 3,008.1 |
| H1 2026 | 701.2 | -5,966.2 | 7,680.5 | 2,415.4 |
| Q2 2026 (derived) | ~17.4 | ~-6,572.2 | ~5,962.2 | ~-592.7 |
| Q4 2025 (derived) | ~1,240.5 | ~4,267.3 | ~-7,709.4 | ~-2,201.6 |

**Observations:**
- **Cash conversion is weak.** H1 2026 operating cash flow was R$701m against R$1,260m of net income, a ratio of about 0.56x. Q2 2026 operating cash flow was nearly zero (about R$17m).
- **Heavy investment is debt-funded.** H1 2026 investing outflows were about R$6.0bn, almost all in Q2 (about R$6.6bn). Financing inflows of R$7.7bn covered them, mostly in Q2 (about R$6.0bn). This pattern suggests a large capex or acquisition program financed with new debt. The filings do not break out the investment type.
- **Operating cash flow barely covers the investment program.** The 2025 full-year operating cash flow of R$3.97bn is well below the cumulative investment outflows.
- **Cash balance is up year-to-date** (+R$2.4bn in H1 2026), but this is entirely from new financing rather than internal generation.

## 4. Key risks and catalysts

**Risks**
1. Financial expense consumes about two-thirds of EBIT. A rise in Brazilian rates (Selic) or in the cost of debt would hit net income quickly.
2. Leverage (liabilities/equity above 3x) and reliance on external financing for investment. Any tightening in credit markets would constrain the program.
3. Weak Q2 operating cash flow. If it persists, dividend capacity and deleveraging become harder.
4. Unexplained equity decline of about R$4bn.
5. Reported 2025 earnings include a one-off gain from discontinued operations.

**Supports**
1. Stable and slightly improving EBIT margins (about 18%).
2. Current ratio steady near 1.5x; short-term liquidity is not stressed.
3. Revenue run-rate modestly above 2025 average.
4. The investment program may drive future regulated-asset or earnings growth, but the filings do not show the returns.

**Timing for the 20-session window (roughly September 2026):** the Q2 2026 ITR was already released on 2026-08-12, so it is not a fresh catalyst. The Q3 2026 ITR is due around November 2026, outside the window. Without price data, I cannot judge whether the stock already reflects these fundamentals or how it will move relative to the Ibovespa.

## 5. Summary assessment

- **Fundamental quality:** mixed. Operating margins are stable and improving, but the balance sheet is more levered, cash conversion is weak, and the investment program is debt-funded.
- **Earnings momentum:** modest. H1 2026 earnings are steady, not accelerating, and 2025 headline EPS overstates the continuing run-rate.
- **For the 4-week relative-return horizon:** no scheduled fundamental catalyst falls inside the window, and the valuation and market-price context is missing. On fundamentals alone, I see no strong basis for an outperformance call versus the Ibovespa. The risk skew is slightly negative because of leverage, weak Q2 cash flow, and sensitivity to interest rates. A **neutral / hold** stance is supported by the data. A trader would need current price, valuation multiples, and a sense of Brazilian rate expectations to refine this.

## Key points summary

| Category | Metric | Latest value | Trend / signal | Implication for traders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Income | Revenue (Q2 2026) | R$13,738.9m | Above 2025 quarterly average (~R$13.0bn) | Modest top-line growth |
| Income | EBIT margin (Q2 2026) | 18.3% | Up from 16.9% (Q3 2025) | Operating improvement |
| Income | Gross margin (Q2 2026) | 26.3% | Stable (24.7%–27.1%) | Stable core economics |
| Income | Financial result (Q2 2026) | -R$1,669.6m | ~70% of EBIT | Interest burden is the key drag |
| Income | Net income (H1 2026) | R$1,259.8m | Annualizes to ~R$2.5bn | Steady, not accelerating |
| Income | EPS (H1 2026) | R$0.724 | Annualized ~R$1.45 | Underlying run-rate below FY2025 headline |
| Income | FY2025 continuing NI | R$2,033.2m | Excludes R$470.7m one-off | Clean base for comparison |
